<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Cases are never created over REST (always 405)"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/exceptions"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



There is deliberately **no `POST /exceptions`**: every case opens
from a consumed fact (ADR 0001), and a repeated fact touches the open
case (occurrence count, `lastSeenAt`) instead of opening another.
Like every `POST` of the fleet it sits behind the idempotency
middleware: the `Idempotency-Key` is demanded first (400
`idempotency-key-required` when absent), then the router answers
`405 method-not-allowed` naming `GET` as the allowed method. The 405
is a deterministic answer and is stored: the same key and request
replays it with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, the same key with a
different request is 409 `idempotency-key-reused`.

<ParamsDetails
  parameters={[{"name":"Idempotency-Key","in":"header","required":true,"description":"Caller-generated unique key (a UUID per logical submit; a retry\nreuses it) that makes a retried request safe. Required on every POST\n(a PUT accepts it too); answered with 400 `idempotency-key-required`\nwhen absent and 400 `idempotency-key-invalid` when it is longer than\n128 characters or not printable ASCII. A replay with the same key and\nthe same request (method, path and body) returns the stored response\nwith the header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; the same key with a\ndifferent request is a 409 `idempotency-key-reused`.\n","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128}}]}
>
  
</ParamsDetails>
